messages:
julie_customer: Hey team — after accepting an org invite this morning, I can call the API with my service token fine but the console throws 403 when I try to switch to project 'acme-proj'. Two people on my team have the same issue. Screenshot pasted. Can you help?

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the minimal repro steps and one curl that returns 403? Also which org/project IDs and user emails?

julie_customer: Steps: 1) Accept invite via email link 2) Sign into console 3) click org > switch project 'acme-proj' 4) get 403. User: julie@acme.com project id: proj-1842 org id: org-77. Curl:```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer s.XYZ" https://console.redwood.ai/projects/proj-1842/switch -v```Response:```HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"forbidden","reason":"role_inheritance_priority_mismatch"}```

ashwin_eng: Thanks — quick check: can you confirm if the same user can access the project via API using the console cookie? (i.e., are console session cookies working different from API tokens?) Also did the customer recently merge AD groups?

julie_customer: API token (PAT) > works. Console session > 403. We did recently merge two AD groups last night (devs-acme + acme-engine).

ken_iam: This reads like a role shadowing / inheritance priority issue after group merge. When two groups map to different org/project roles and the system has an inherited-deny tag precedence, the console UI enforces the final effective permission which can be deny even if API token for service principal has explicit allow. I need to run a diagnostics check — maria, can you run the internal iam checker for julie?

maria_support: Running quick diag now: `/internal/diagnostics/iam-check --user julie@acme.com --project proj-1842 --verbose` Output snippet:```
user: julie@acme.com
project: proj-1842
bindings:
  - group: acme-engine -> role: project/editor (inherited from org-77)
  - group: devs-acme -> role: project/viewer (explicit on project)
conflicts:
  - inheritance_priority: org-level binding (acme-engine) marked as 'deny' during legacy migration
effective: DENY (console-enforced)
```

ken_iam: Confirmed. AD group merge created overlapping bindings and the legacy migration accidentally set the org-level binding priority to deny for that principal. Workaround: temporarily give julie a direct project-level role while we fix the mapping. Use: `rbac assign --project proj-1842 --member "user:julie@acme.com" --role project/viewer --expires 3600`

maria_support: I applied the temporary assign for 1 hour and asked the IdP team to run SCIM resync with the new group canonical name. Also queued a migration fix to clear the legacy deny flag.

ci-bot: job/iam-scim-resync started by ops_automation at 3334510200

ops_automation: SCIM resync completed — 18 groups reconciled, 2 changed: devs-acme -> devs-acme-new, acme-engine -> acme-engine (merged).

ci-bot: job/iam-migration-fix applied at 3334510400 (migration v2026.03.15-fix-shadowing) — removed legacy deny flag for org-77 bindings.

maria_support: Can you retry switching now, julie? I removed the temp role since migration applied.

julie_customer: Switching works now, no 403. Access looks correct and team members can switch too. Thanks! :raised_hands:

maria_support: Great — root cause: group-merge + legacy migration set an organ-level deny priority, which shadowed project allow rules for console sessions. Action items: ken will add a guard in the migration to detect merged group mappings, ops will keep SCIM change log for 48h so we can roll back quickly. Closing unless it reappears.

ken_iam: Filed GH issue: redwood/infra#4122 — detect and warn on overlapping group->role mappings during migration.

maria_support: If anyone hits this in the short term, workaround is the `rbac assign` temp grant or run SCIM resync. Reopen thread if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
